fixes.explanation: It's the other way around. The spies tell Joshua, “There is no need to send all the people; two or three thousand men are enough to go up and attack Ai.” They say Ai's people are so few that Joshua need not wear out everyone. That's a small plan said with big confidence, and I know that confidence from the inside.

Verse 4 says about three thousand men went up, but they fled before the men of Ai. The spies had just called Ai's people so few. I think that report made running the last thing anyone had in mind. The text says they fled, and in verse 5 the men of Ai chase them from the gate.

I get why this one tempts. The spies did say two or three thousand men were enough, so capturing Ai sounds like the plan. But the text says the men went up and fled before the men of Ai. Capturing Ai never happens in this scene.

Joshua says, “If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!” (Joshua 7:7). He says it out loud to the Lord GOD, with his face on the ground. I think his heart is heavy. Notice where he looks: back across the river.
Egypt doesn't show up in Joshua's words here. He wishes they had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan. That's the wish he brings to the Lord GOD. Egypt isn't part of it.

I think Joshua's worry points the other way. He says the Canaanites and all who live in the land will surround Israel and wipe out its name. In his words, they're the ones closing in. Running away in fear isn't what he pictures them doing.

Achan says he saw a beautiful cloak from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. Then he says, “I coveted them and took them.” He rattles off the list, weights and all. I bet that list had been running through his head for a while.

Achan doesn't mention a crown, a sword or a shield. What he names is a beautiful cloak from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. He says he saw them among the spoils, coveted them and took them. That's a different pile of loot than the one on this answer.

Bronze pots and iron tools aren't on Achan's list. He says he saw among the spoils a beautiful cloak from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. Those are the things he coveted and took. I'd say that's quite a step up from kitchenware.

Not quite. Achan says the things are hidden in the ground inside his tent, with the silver underneath. So the hiding spot is in his tent, not somewhere outside the camp. The messengers run to the tent and there it all is, just as he said.

They took the things from inside the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and spread them out before the LORD. What Achan had hidden in the ground is now laid out in the open. Verse 22 says it was all there in his tent, with the silver underneath, so his confession matched what they found. The hiding is over.
